items.title: Sheila Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Middleburgh, New York, May 11, 2002
items.q: I’d go upstairs and [sings] Softique, the stuff you take a bath in. So I’m singing about Softique to “Body and Soul.”

ctx.x: The years you spent with a day job, did that make the gigs and recordings you were able to do more precious?

Yeah. I think so, for me I would say yes. I never thought of myself as a part time singer because I didn’t do it full time. I worked in an office for two reasons. I had a daughter to support, I didn’t want her raised the way I was raised as a young kid which was in a very, very poverty stricken household. So I kept that day job. They knew that I loved the music and so I could take leaves of absences if I got gigs, or always my vacation time was to do music. I’d save my vacation time and take it in days. The…

I was not depending on this music to support me. I was depending on this music, I mean financially, I was depending on this music to support me emotionally and keep me alive, which it did. I had a spiritual awakening when I was quite young and which said to me I’ll support this music until it can support me and maybe it will never support me financially. But I will support it because I believe in it. And so in so doing and with that attitude I never had a better attitude about working, I never was cynical, I…
